report.summary: Chunk 4 of 4: check, render_text, main, and helper functions for inventory module.
risks: _describe_drift | medium | If both old and fresh have same head and statuses but derived fields differ, the function appends a generic message 'the derived half differs...' which may be misleading if no actual difference exists. | Verify with a test case where old_feats and new_feats are identical but other blocks differ.

handoff.purpose: Provide check, render_text, main, and helper functions for inventory.

symbols.name: check
symbols.note: Gate mode: returns ok/false with problems list.

symbols.name: _by_key
symbols.note: Returns derived fields keyed by module.

symbols.name: _describe_drift
symbols.note: Generates drift description between stored and fresh.

claims.text: Gate mode. Writes nothing; returns ``{"ok": bool, "problems": [...]}``.
claims.why: The function returns a dict with 'ok' and 'problems' keys, and does not perform any file writes.

claims.text: Four ways to fail, in the order a reader needs them: 1. there is no inventory, or it cannot be parsed; 2. it was written by a different schema; 3. its digest does not cover its own derived fields -- somebody edited the mechanical half by hand; 4. regenerating it now would change something -- it is STALE, and the diff says exactly how.
claims.why: The code checks for load failure (1), schema mismatch (2), digest failure (3), and drift (4) in that order.

claims.text: Every feature's DERIVED half, keyed by module (or by detector for the module-less stale entries). The human fields are dropped so a note cannot read as drift.
claims.why: The function iterates areas/features, uses module or detector:reason as key, and filters out FEATURE_HUMAN_FIELDS.

claims.text: Field-level, not just status-level. A module whose importers or reaching entry point changed is a real difference, and reporting it as 'something differs, go diff the file yourself' is how a gate stops being read.
claims.why: The function compares old_feats and new_feats field by field (excluding status) and reports changed fields.

claims.text: the derived half differs from a fresh scan (no headline difference; compare the file with --json)
claims.why: If no other differences found, this message is appended to out.

claims.text: Mechanical fields are rewritten every run; human notes are carried forward and excluded from the digest.
claims.why: The chunk does not contain the build or harvest functions that implement this behavior.

observations.what: Function check uses load and build, but load is defined elsewhere; build is defined elsewhere in this file but not shown.

In _describe_drift, if both old and fresh have same head and statuses but derived fields differ, the function appends a generic message 'the derived half differs...' which may be misleading if no actual difference exists.
The main function's --json path calls load and build but does not use the 'old' variable for anything other than initial load; it always rebuilds fresh.
